text: Snowflake's architecture is often described as a 'hybrid' model. What does this mean?

options.A: It combines on-premise and cloud infrastructure
options.B: It uses a shared-data architecture — storage is shared and centralized, while compute is independent and scalable (combining benefits of shared-disk and shared-nothing)
options.C: It runs on both relational and NoSQL engines simultaneously
options.D: It splits workloads between batch and streaming layers

explanation: Snowflake's hybrid (shared-data) architecture separates storage from compute. Storage is centralized and shared (like shared-disk), but compute clusters (warehouses) are independent and don't compete for resources (like shared-nothing). This gives scalability and concurrency.

text: The Cloud Services layer uses compute resources for metadata operations, query compilation, and access control. Under what condition does this become a billable cost?

options.A: Always — every query incurs Cloud Services charges
options.B: Never — Cloud Services are free
options.C: Only when Cloud Services consumption exceeds 10% of the daily total warehouse consumption
options.D: Only when the account exceeds 1000 queries per day

explanation: Cloud Services credits are included (free) up to 10% of daily warehouse consumption. Only the EXCESS beyond 10% is billed. Most normal workloads never exceed this threshold.

text: Which Snowflake layer stores the metadata about micro-partitions (min/max values, null counts, distinct counts)?

options.A: The Storage layer alongside the data files
options.B: The Compute layer in SSD cache
options.C: The Cloud Services layer — metadata is managed centrally for query optimization and pruning
options.D: A separate metadata database provisioned per account

explanation: Metadata (min/max per column, row count, null count, distinct values) is stored and managed in the Cloud Services layer. This enables pruning decisions BEFORE data is scanned, and allows metadata-only queries (like COUNT*) to return without using a warehouse.

text: Which TWO features are ONLY available on Business Critical Edition or higher? (Select TWO)

options.A: Multi-cluster warehouses
options.B: PrivateLink support
options.D: Materialized views

explanation: Business Critical+: PrivateLink, Tri-Secret Secure, HIPAA/PHI compliance, ISMAP. Enterprise+: multi-cluster warehouses, materialized views, dynamic masking, 90-day Time Travel, Search Optimization.

text: An organization wants HIPAA compliance and PHI data handling in Snowflake. Which is the MINIMUM required edition?

options.A: Standard
options.B: Enterprise
options.D: VPS (Virtual Private Snowflake)

explanation: HIPAA/PHI compliance requires Business Critical Edition or higher. Business Critical adds healthcare-grade security features including HIPAA support, PrivateLink, and Tri-Secret Secure.

text: The Snowsight Activity tab shows two main types of information. What are they?

options.A: Warehouse credits and storage costs
options.B: Query History and Copy History (data loading operations)
options.D: Task execution and pipe status

explanation: The Snowsight Activity tab shows: Query History (executed queries, duration, warehouse) and Copy History (COPY INTO operations, files loaded). This is a commonly tested fact about Snowsight capabilities.

text: An engineer needs to download a file from an internal stage to their local machine. Which command and tool combination is required?

options.A: COPY INTO from Snowsight
options.B: GET command from SnowSQL or a programmatic driver — it downloads from internal stages to the local filesystem
options.D: EXPORT command from Snowsight

explanation: GET downloads files from an internal stage to the local filesystem. Like PUT, it requires a client with filesystem access — SnowSQL or programmatic drivers. GET does not work from Snowsight or with external stages.

text: What is the difference between SnowSQL and the Snowflake CLI (snow)?

options.A: They are the same tool with different names
options.B: SnowSQL executes SQL interactively. The Snowflake CLI (snow) manages Snowflake objects, deploys apps, and performs administrative tasks — it is NOT a SQL client.
options.C: SnowSQL is deprecated; the Snowflake CLI replaces it entirely
options.D: SnowSQL is for Linux; the Snowflake CLI is for Windows

explanation: SnowSQL: command-line SQL client (execute queries, PUT/GET files). Snowflake CLI (snow): object management, deploy Streamlit apps, manage Notebooks, run dbt — NOT for ad-hoc SQL. Different tools, different purposes.

text: A user creates a temporary table in their session. What happens to the table when the session ends?

options.A: The table persists until explicitly dropped
options.B: The table is automatically DROPPED when the session ends — it is invisible to other sessions
options.C: The table converts to a transient table
options.D: The table remains for 24 hours then is dropped

explanation: Temporary tables are session-scoped. They are only visible to the creating session and are automatically dropped when that session ends. They have 0-1 day Time Travel and 0 days Fail-safe.

text: What is the scope of a database role compared to an account role?

options.A: Database roles and account roles have identical scope
options.B: A database role is scoped to a SINGLE database only and cannot hold privileges outside that database. An account role exists at account level and can hold privileges on any object.
options.C: Database roles are more powerful because they bypass schema permissions
options.D: Account roles only work within a single schema

explanation: Database roles: scoped to one database, can only hold privileges within that database, useful for sharing via shares. Account roles: exist at account level, can hold privileges on any object across databases.

text: An engineer lists files on a stage using LIST @my_stage. Can this command be executed from Snowsight?

options.A: No — LIST requires SnowSQL like PUT/GET
options.B: Yes — LIST (and REMOVE) work from any SQL client including Snowsight. Only PUT and GET require local filesystem access.
options.C: No — LIST only works with external stages
options.D: Yes, but only for user stages

explanation: LIST and REMOVE work from any SQL client (Snowsight, SnowSQL, drivers) because they operate on server-side stage objects. Only PUT and GET require local filesystem access (SnowSQL/drivers only).

text: What are the THREE types of internal stages in Snowflake?

options.A: Primary, secondary, and tertiary
options.B: User stage (@~), table stage (@%table_name), and named internal stage (@my_stage)
options.D: Compressed, uncompressed, and encrypted stages

explanation: Three internal stage types: User stage (@~ — per user, auto-created), Table stage (@%table_name — per table, auto-created), Named internal stage (@my_stage — explicitly created, can have file formats and directory tables).

text: A file format object is created with TYPE=CSV, SKIP_HEADER=1, FIELD_DELIMITER='|'. What is the primary benefit of creating a named file format object?

options.A: It compresses files automatically
options.B: It is REUSABLE — the same named object can be referenced across multiple COPY INTO commands and stages without repeating options
options.C: It validates data quality before loading
options.D: It encrypts file contents

explanation: Named file format objects are reusable definitions. Instead of specifying TYPE, DELIMITER, SKIP_HEADER etc. inline every time, you reference the named object. This ensures consistency and reduces errors.

text: A warehouse is created with INITIALLY_SUSPENDED = TRUE. What happens immediately after creation?

options.A: The warehouse starts running and consuming credits
options.B: The warehouse is created in SUSPENDED state — it does NOT consume credits until resumed or AUTO_RESUME triggers
options.C: The warehouse enters a provisioning queue
options.D: An error occurs because warehouses must start in running state

explanation: INITIALLY_SUSPENDED = TRUE (also the default in some creation flows) creates the warehouse without starting it. No credits are consumed. It will resume when a query is submitted (if AUTO_RESUME = TRUE) or manually resumed.

text: A running warehouse is resized from Medium to Large while queries are actively executing. What happens to those running queries?

options.A: They are cancelled and must be resubmitted
options.B: They continue on existing resources. New resources are provisioned but only used for QUEUED and future queries — running queries are NOT interrupted.
options.C: They immediately get more resources from the resize
options.D: The resize is blocked until current queries finish

explanation: Resizing a running warehouse does NOT interrupt or affect currently executing queries. New compute resources are provisioned and used only for statements already in queue or submitted after provisioning completes.

text: What is the credit-per-hour rate for a 4X-Large warehouse?

options.A: 64 credits/hour
options.B: 128 credits/hour
options.D: 32 credits/hour

explanation: Credit rates double with each size: XS=1, S=2, M=4, L=8, XL=16, 2XL=32, 3XL=64, 4XL=128 credits/hour. 4X-Large = 128 credits/hour.

text: Multi-cluster warehouse in Maximized mode with MIN_CLUSTER_COUNT = 3 and MAX_CLUSTER_COUNT = 3. What does this mean?

options.A: The warehouse starts with 1 cluster and scales up to 3 based on demand
options.B: Exactly 3 clusters run at ALL times — no auto-scaling occurs. This provides constant high concurrency.
options.C: 3 clusters run during business hours only
options.D: A maximum of 3 queries can run simultaneously

explanation: Maximized mode with MIN=MAX=3 means exactly 3 clusters run continuously. No scaling up or down occurs. This is used when constant, predictable concurrency is needed and cost is less of a concern.

text: A warehouse has AUTO_RESUME = TRUE and AUTO_SUSPEND = 60. A user submits a query while the warehouse is suspended. What sequence occurs?

options.A: The query fails because the warehouse is suspended
options.B: The warehouse automatically resumes, provisions resources, executes the query, then auto-suspends after 60 seconds of inactivity
options.C: The query queues indefinitely until an admin resumes the warehouse
options.D: The query is redirected to Cloud Services

explanation: AUTO_RESUME = TRUE means the warehouse automatically starts when a query is submitted. After execution, it waits 60 seconds of inactivity (AUTO_SUSPEND = 60) then suspends. The user experiences a brief delay during provisioning.

text: Micro-partitions store data in what format?

options.A: Row-oriented format optimized for OLTP
options.B: Columnar format — data within each micro-partition is organized by column for efficient analytical scanning
options.D: JSON documents

explanation: Micro-partitions store data in columnar format. This enables efficient analytical scans (only read needed columns), better compression (similar values stored together), and effective pruning via column-level min/max metadata.

text: What is the uncompressed size range of a single micro-partition?

options.D: 500 MB - 1 GB

explanation: Micro-partitions are 50-500 MB uncompressed (significantly smaller when compressed). Snowflake automatically determines the optimal size — users cannot configure it.

text: An engineer creates a clustering key on columns (region, order_date). After heavy DML over several weeks, they want to check if the table needs reclustering. Which function should they use?

options.A: SHOW TABLE STATISTICS
options.B: SYSTEM$CLUSTERING_INFORMATION — returns clustering depth, partition overlap, and clustering ratio
options.D: TABLE_STORAGE_METRICS

explanation: SYSTEM$CLUSTERING_INFORMATION returns: average_depth (overlap), clustering_ratio, and partition details. This tells you if reclustering is needed (high depth = poor clustering).

text: A dynamic table is defined with: CREATE DYNAMIC TABLE dt AS SELECT ... FROM t1 JOIN t2 ON ... TARGET_LAG = '5 minutes'. Which statement is TRUE?

options.A: This fails because dynamic tables cannot reference JOINs
options.B: This succeeds — dynamic tables support JOINs and Snowflake refreshes the table to stay within 5 minutes of source freshness
options.C: This succeeds but only with FULL refresh mode
options.D: This fails because the minimum TARGET_LAG is 10 minutes

explanation: Dynamic tables support JOINs, aggregations, and multi-table queries (unlike materialized views). TARGET_LAG = 5 minutes means Snowflake ensures the table's data is never more than 5 minutes stale. Minimum lag is 1 minute.

text: How does a secure view differ from a standard view in terms of the query optimizer?

options.A: No difference — both are optimized identically
options.B: Secure views bypass SOME query optimizations to prevent data leakage through timing or row-count inference — this can impact performance
options.C: Secure views are always faster because they use dedicated compute
options.D: Standard views cannot be optimized

explanation: Secure views disable certain optimizations (like predicate pushdown past the view boundary) that could leak information. This means secure views may perform slower than standard views. The tradeoff is security vs. performance.

text: A table is defined as an external table pointing to files in S3. Can you run INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE on it?

options.A: Yes — external tables support full DML
options.B: No — external tables are READ-ONLY. The data is managed externally and Snowflake only reads it.
options.D: Yes, but only via stored procedures

explanation: External tables are read-only in Snowflake. The data lives in customer-managed cloud storage. Snowflake can query it but cannot modify it. DML must be done outside Snowflake on the source files.

text: Which TWO table types have ZERO Fail-safe days? (Select TWO)

options.A: Permanent tables
options.B: Transient tables
options.D: Dynamic tables

explanation: Transient and temporary tables have 0 days Fail-safe (reducing storage costs). Permanent tables have 7 days. External tables have N/A (data is external). Dynamic tables behave like permanent tables for Fail-safe.

text: In which supported languages can Snowpark DataFrames be written?

options.A: Python only
options.B: Python, Java, and Scala
options.D: SQL and Python only

explanation: Snowpark supports three languages: Python, Java, and Scala. All produce DataFrames that are lazily evaluated and execute on the warehouse. R is not supported by Snowpark (use it via external functions or SPCS).

text: Where does Snowpark code execute — on the client machine or on the Snowflake warehouse?

options.A: On the client machine that submitted the code
options.B: On the Snowflake virtual warehouse — Snowpark pushes computation to the server, not the client
options.C: On a dedicated Snowpark cluster separate from warehouses
options.D: Half on client, half on server

explanation: Snowpark code executes on the Snowflake warehouse, not the client. The client only builds and submits the execution plan. This is a key exam trap — 'Snowpark runs on the client' is FALSE.

text: Snowflake Notebooks support which cell types?

options.A: SQL only
options.B: Python only
options.C: SQL, Python, and Markdown — enabling mixed-language analysis in a single notebook
options.D: SQL and Java

explanation: Snowflake Notebooks support SQL cells, Python cells, and Markdown cells. They can run on a virtual warehouse (SQL/Snowpark) or on Container Runtime (SPCS) for GPU/custom packages.

text: Snowflake Notebooks can run on two different compute backends. What are they?

options.A: Standard warehouse and Snowpark-optimized warehouse
options.B: Virtual warehouse (for SQL/Snowpark) and Container Runtime powered by Snowpark Container Services (for custom packages and GPUs)
options.D: CPU cluster and GPU cluster in the same warehouse

explanation: Notebooks run on: (1) Virtual warehouses for SQL and Snowpark pushdown queries, or (2) Container Runtime (SPCS) for custom packages, GPUs, and ML workloads. Container Runtime provides flexible compute with pip install support.

text: Cortex Search provides what type of search capability?

options.A: SQL full-text search only
options.B: Hybrid keyword + vector (semantic) search over text data
options.D: Database schema search

explanation: Cortex Search provides hybrid search combining traditional keyword matching with vector/semantic similarity search. It indexes text data and retrieves relevant results using both approaches for better recall and precision.

text: A Model Registry in Snowflake allows you to store trained ML models. What can you do with a registered model?

options.A: Only store it for documentation purposes
options.B: Store, version, deploy, and run inference on trained models — including calling them from SQL
options.C: Only use it from Python clients
options.D: Automatically retrain it on new data

explanation: The Model Registry stores, versions, and deploys ML models. Registered models can be called from SQL for inference, enabling predictions directly in queries without external infrastructure.

text: An ETL pipeline runs nightly at 2am and takes 45 minutes. It uses a dedicated Large warehouse. What is the recommended AUTO_SUSPEND setting?

options.A: AUTO_SUSPEND = 0 (never suspend)
options.B: AUTO_SUSPEND = 60 (1 minute) — suspend quickly after the batch completes to minimize idle credits
options.D: AUTO_SUSPEND = 3600 (1 hour)

explanation: For batch/ETL workloads with predictable end times, a short AUTO_SUSPEND (60 seconds) is cost-effective. The warehouse runs during the 45-min job, then suspends 1 minute after completion, minimizing wasted credits.

text: A query is submitted to a suspended warehouse with AUTO_RESUME = FALSE. What happens?

options.A: The warehouse auto-resumes and runs the query
options.B: The query FAILS with an error — the warehouse cannot be used when suspended and AUTO_RESUME is disabled
options.D: The query runs on Cloud Services instead

explanation: With AUTO_RESUME = FALSE, a suspended warehouse does NOT automatically start. Queries submitted to it will fail. An administrator must manually resume it with ALTER WAREHOUSE ... RESUME.

text: VPS (Virtual Private Snowflake) edition provides what unique capability compared to Business Critical?

options.A: Faster query performance
options.B: A completely isolated Snowflake environment — dedicated infrastructure with no shared compute or storage with other customers
options.D: Automatic query optimization

explanation: VPS provides a fully isolated, dedicated Snowflake deployment. Unlike other editions where Snowflake infrastructure is multi-tenant, VPS gives complete isolation. It also restricts sharing to support-mediated only.

text: A stream tracks changes to a table. What metadata columns does a standard stream add to track change types?

options.A: CHANGE_TYPE only
options.B: METADATA$ACTION (INSERT/DELETE), METADATA$ISUPDATE (TRUE/FALSE), and METADATA$ROW_ID
options.D: OPERATION and VERSION

explanation: Standard streams add: METADATA$ACTION (INSERT or DELETE), METADATA$ISUPDATE (TRUE if part of an UPDATE — shows as DELETE+INSERT pair), and METADATA$ROW_ID (unique row identifier).

text: What is the NOT NULL constraint's unique status among Snowflake constraints?

options.A: It is informational only like all other constraints
options.B: NOT NULL is the ONLY constraint that is actually ENFORCED in Snowflake — all others (PK, FK, UNIQUE) are informational only
options.D: It only works on STRING columns

explanation: NOT NULL is the only enforced constraint. PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, and UNIQUE are all informational/metadata-only — they do NOT prevent violations. This is critical for the exam.

text: Snowpark Container Services (SPCS) allows you to run containerized applications within Snowflake. What do you need to run a service?

options.A: A virtual warehouse and a Docker image
options.B: An image repository (for your container image), a compute pool (VM nodes), and a service specification (YAML)
options.C: Only a stored procedure with container support
options.D: An external Kubernetes cluster connected via API integration

explanation: SPCS requires: (1) an image repository to store your OCI container images, (2) a compute pool (VM nodes with CPU/GPU), and (3) a service specification (YAML) defining containers, endpoints, and configuration.

text: What happens if a warehouse begins provisioning but some compute resources FAIL to provision during startup?

options.A: The warehouse stays suspended until all resources are available
options.B: Snowflake starts processing queries once 50% or more of requested resources are provisioned, while repairing the failed resources
options.D: All queries are cancelled and an alert is sent

explanation: If some resources fail during provisioning, Snowflake repairs them while starting query processing once 50%+ resources are available. This ensures queries are not blocked by partial provisioning failures.

text: A secure materialized view exists on a table. Can it be shared via Secure Data Sharing?

options.A: No — materialized views cannot be shared under any circumstances
options.B: Yes — secure materialized views CAN be shared. Only non-secure materialized views cannot.
options.C: Yes, but only on VPS edition
options.D: No — only regular secure views can be shared

explanation: Secure materialized views CAN be shared. The rule is that only SECURE objects can be added to shares — secure views, secure UDFs, secure materialized views, tables, and external tables. Non-secure materialized views cannot.

text: Cortex AI has a function called COMPLETE that accepts a prompt and returns generated text. What type of AI model powers this function?

options.A: A traditional statistical model
options.B: A Large Language Model (LLM) — COMPLETE sends prompts to an LLM and returns generated text responses
options.D: A computer vision model

explanation: CORTEX.COMPLETE uses a Large Language Model (LLM) to generate text from prompts. You can specify different model sizes (e.g., mistral-large, llama3-70b). It runs on Snowflake's serverless AI infrastructure.
